newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Octava NFI eyes portfolio of 15-20 firms.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Octava NFI eyes portfolio of 15-20 firms.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Fund Octava SA (NFI no. 8) wants to limit the number of companies in which it holds significant shareholdings to 15-20, down from the present 30, the fund's president said on Monday.
"Given the size of the fund its optimum portfolio should encompass 15-20 firms and we want to reach this level as quickly as possible," Piotr Rymaszewski told Reuters in an interview.
Octava now has in its portfolio 30 companies in which it has 33 percent stakes and minority shareholdings in several hundred companies, ranging from 1.93 percent to 9.64 percent.
Rymaszewski said Octava did not plan any flotations for this year.
"We do not plan to list any of our companies on the bourse. In my opinion they are not ready yet for listing and the exchange is also not the only source of capital," he said.
Rymaszewski said the fund was in talks with several prospective investors, who might take stakes in firms in its portfolio.
"We are in talks with potential investors and for example a strategic investor is not ruled out in Pollena Lechia (cosmetics maker) as interest is rather high," he said.
He added that Octava did not plan to pay a dividend in the near future. In the first quarter of 1997, Octava reported a net profit of 7.8 million zlotys.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-sized companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trading on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
